messages.subject: fwd & rev namespaces?
parts:
On 8/8/13 5:55 PM, Daniel Lee wrote:
> Thanks. This email helps a lot.
>
> On Wed, Aug 7, 2013 at 6:29 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com <mailto:ca...@alias-i.com>> wrote:
>
> I'm still not sure if it makes sense to introduce fwd and
> rev namespaces. I understand now that we need to define
> their ops in a namespace where we can use argument-dependent
> lookup OR we need to make sure all of the fwd and rev versions
> are proper specializations rather than overloads so that we
> can import just the stan::math version.
>
>
> Hmmm. I don't think my head is fully around that paragraph. I think if we really want the auto diff library to exist on
> its own, I would think that it'd be good to include either the reverse header, the forward header, or both and just use
> the stan::math namespace. I'm not sure I'm convinced about the namespace thing, though.

The question is how do we pick up the auto-diff versions?

If they're in their own namespace, such as stan::agrad, then
the right versions get picked up by argument-dependent lookup.

Suppose foo is defined in stan::math::foo and we try to define:

template <typename T>
T two_foo(const T& x) {
using stan::math::foo;
return 2 * foo(x);
}

So we only have a using statement for stan::math. But if
foo(stan::agrad::var) is defined in the stan::agrad
namespace, then argument-dependent lookup will bring in the
right version of foo will be used for two_foo.

This approach also works for std::exp, defined in std namespace.

For our own functions, we could alternatively define the agrad::fwd
version of foo in the stan::math namespace and then use template
specializations or overloading. Template specializations are
problematic for functions without C++-11.

So I think we should just continue to define agrad versions of
functions in the agrad namespace. It's consistent with what we
have to do with std:: functions.

- Bob
